title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 40-43). Let (S, 𝒯) be a topological space and T ⊂ S a 𝒯-closed subset with open complement U = S∖T. Let 𝒯'_0 be a topology on T finer than 𝒯|T. Let 𝒞 be the class of topologies on S that are finer than 𝒯 and induce 𝒯'_0 on T; from the proof these also leave 𝒯|U unchanged and keep T closed. The proposition (a, b, c on p. 41) says the following.
- 𝒞 has a coarsest element 𝒯'.
- The closed sets of 𝒯' are the sets X = B ∪ cl_𝒯(X∩U), where B is 𝒯'_0-closed in T.
- Equivalently, closed sets correspond to pairs (B, A_U), with A_U closed in U and cl_𝒯(A_U) ∩ T ⊂ B.

Part (d): if both topologies are Alexandrov ('ultra-topologies', i.e. preorders), so is 𝒯'. Its preorder is ≤_{𝒯'_0} on T and ≤_𝒯 on U. For x ∈ T and y ∈ U, x ≤ y iff x ≤_𝒯 y. Nothing of U lies below a point of T.

Part (e): pass to the posets (T0 quotients) I', I, with canonical map φ: I' → I. J ⊂ I is the closed image of T, J' = φ^{-1}(J) and U' = I'∖J'. Page 41 had wrongly called the topology T̄' on I' the 'plus fine'.

This page restates the characterisation as four conditions:
- (i) T̄' is finer than the pulled-back topology 𝒯̃ and induces T̄|J' on J'.
- (ii) T̄'|U' = 𝒯̃|U'.
- (iii) φ|U' is a homeomorphism U' → U (the earlier word 'bijection' is crossed out).
- (iv) The topology of I is the final topology for I' → I and J → I.

Condition (iv) says I is the pushout I' ⊔_{J'} J. Without it one gets the trivial solution satisfying (i)-(ii): the sum topology on I' = J' ⊔ U', corresponding to I itself being J ⊔ U. The margin notes 'C'est faux… v. 48' and the circled remark say the earlier formulation was wrong. They add that satisfying (i)-(iv) amounts to T̄' ∈ 𝒞, with the main remark deferred to p. 48.

Demonstration of (a, b, c):
- The sets listed in c) are exactly those satisfying conditions 1°-3° of b), and their representation is unique.
- These sets are stable under arbitrary intersections and finite unions, so they are the closed sets of a topology.
- They are stable under arbitrary unions when (T, 𝒯'_0) and (S, 𝒯) are Alexandrov, giving the Alexandrov claim.
- Page 43 completes the proof: the topology lies in 𝒞 and is its coarsest element. Any 𝒯'' ∈ 𝒞 has B closed in T, T closed, and cl_𝒯(X∩U) 𝒯-closed, so every 𝒯'-closed set is 𝒯''-closed.

Modern reading: this is the recollement (gluing) of a topology along a closed/open decomposition. One keeps the open part and refines the closed stratum, and the coarsest glued topology uses the closure functor as gluing map. In the finite-poset ('figures') case this is refining the closed stratum of a finite stratified space by a pushout of posets.
errors: Page 41 called T̄' 'la plus fine' topology inducing T̄|J' on J'. It is the coarsest (least fine) one, as the proof on p. 43 shows. Grothendieck's margin note 'C'est faux… v. 48' and the change of wording on this page acknowledge a mistake in the formulation.

Checking (iv): for the coarsest T̄', a subset F ⊂ I whose preimage is closed and whose trace on J is closed is indeed closed in I, since cl(F∩U) ⊂ F. For strictly finer members of 𝒞, (iv) fails. So (i)-(iv) seem to characterize T̄' correctly, though the exact correction made on p. 48 cannot be verified from this page.

Stability under finite unions needs closure to commute with finite unions (true). Stability under arbitrary unions in the Alexandrov case needs closure to commute with arbitrary unions, which holds in Alexandrov spaces. The text's 'clair'/'id.' is acceptable.

ideas.what: Coarsest topology on S finer than 𝒯 that induces a prescribed finer topology on a closed subset T and keeps the open complement. Its closed sets are B ∪ cl(X∩U).
ideas.modern_name: Recollement (gluing) of topologies / open-closed decomposition, topological shadow of recollement of topoi
ideas.usually_credited_to: Artin-Grothendieck-Verdier (SGA 4 IV 9.5, recollement of topoi); classical point-set topology
ideas.where_published: SGA 4, Exposé IV §9.5 (recollement of topoi along open/closed subtopoi)

ideas.what: Description of the resulting specialization preorder in the Alexandrov case: refine on T, keep on U, cross relations as in 𝒯.
ideas.modern_name: Gluing of finite posets / finite stratified spaces

ideas.what: Characterization of the glued topology on posets by a pushout/final-topology condition: I = I' ⊔_{J'} J, with φ an isomorphism over the open part.
ideas.modern_name: Pushout of finite T0 spaces; modification (refinement) of a closed stratum

deep.surprise_reason: A routine point-set lemma (recollement of a topology along a closed subset, specialised to Alexandrov/finite posets) with a self-correction. It is a technical step in the 'algèbre des figures' programme, with no new idea beyond what SGA 4 recollement and folklore on finite spaces contain.
transcription_corrections: Bottom line should read 'stable par réunion quelconque s'il en est ainsi pour (T, 𝒯'_0), (S, 𝒯)', i.e. with 𝒯'_0 (primed) as on p. 41. The leading 'S'est' is probably 'Il est' or 'L'ens. est'.
'la moins fine des topo. ∈ 𝒞' uses script/underlined 𝒞 (the class of admissible topologies), not 𝒯; similarly 'qu'elle est dans 𝒞'.
'Il est clair que les ens. décrits dans c)': the [?] [?] is likely 'décrits'.
In (iv) the parenthesis reads 'I' muni de T̄', J muni de T̄|J'. In the trivial-solution clause, 'si I lui-même est muni de la topo. J ⊔ U'; the small 'I∖J' under U glosses U = I∖J.
The top-left margin probably reads 'C'est faux, ceci signifie que … (iii)(iv) … condition … plus fine ! v. 48 … i.e. T̄' ∈ 𝒞', i.e. a self-correction referring forward to p. 48.
